newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - TOBACCO TO PUFF UP REMGRO H1 SHR.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - TOBACCO TO PUFF UP REMGRO H1 SHR.

text.p: Tobacco profits will once again fire robust earnings growth at South Africa's Rembrandt Group Ltd, hemmed in only slightly by poor performances from some industrial interests, analysts said on Friday.
The investment holding company is due to post results for the six months to end-September on Monday.

Analysts polled by Reuters expect earnings per share before exceptional items, including the share of net income retained by associates, to climb to between 160 and 162.6 cents with consensus at 161 cents -- 26 percent up on last year's 128 cents.
An interim dividend of 29.4 cents a share was declared in August, 20 percent up on last year's 24.5 cents.

"The tobacco interests will give them the push again. Despite the hassles they have had from anti-smoking lobbies, third world consumption of cigarettes is still increasing," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Dave Southey, an analyst at brokerage Edey Rogers estimated tobacco profits would be up around 35 percent.

But without the burden of heavy losses at its poultry investment, Rainbow Chicken Ltd , and Rainbow parent, timber company Hunt Leuchars & Hepburn (HLH), Remgro's bottomline would have been higher, analysts said.
"The industrial interests are a mess with HL&H and Rainbow Ltd," Southey said.
Rainbow recently reported a 164.4 million rand loss for the six months to September 30 due to low poultry prices and rising feed costs, a situation aggravated by the fall in the rand.
The loss dragged HL&H into the red with the group posting a first half attributable loss of 11.7 million rand. Remgro owns an 82.9 percent stake in HL&H parent, Huntcor .

Remgro's other industrial interests, engineering firms Metkor Ltd and Dorbyl Ltd, beverage companies Stellenbosch Farmers Winery Ltd and Distillers Corp (South Africa) Ltd , and medical supplier Medi-Clinic Corp Ltd had done well, analysts said.
Southey said a further boon for Remgro was its sizeable cash pile. "Interest rates are quite high so they will earn a lot on their cash balances," he said.
Mining interests with the exception of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd , would also contribute to Remgro's growth.
Other mining investments include Gencor Ltd , in which Remgro holds a 13.7 percent stake, and diamond producer Trans Hex Group Ltd .
